title: DAO Resolutions authorize named legal entities per counterparty, giving Grove's onchain governance effect in the offchain legal world
content:
A.6.1.1.2.3.6 records that "Grove has formally agreed to the DAO Resolutions recorded herein," and the seven entries share a precise form: a date, a named set of legal entities, a named counterparty or transaction, and an IPFS link to the resolution text. **Grove Foundation and Bamboo Grove Ltd** are authorized to onboard to FalconX (.6.1, .6.5), with Ripple, Agora and Paxos (.6.3) and with Wintermute (.6.4); **Bamboo Grove** alone to onboard with Ethena, together with an approved Deed Poll (.6.2); **Grove Foundation and Grove (BVI) Ltd** for Project Grove (.6.6); and **Grove Foundation and Cedar Grove Ltd** to subscribe for and purchase Class B notes issued by Galaxy CLO 2025-1 LLC (.6.7).

Three things follow from the pattern.

First, Grove is not only an onchain Agent. It operates through a set of distinct legal entities, and the pairing is not arbitrary — Bamboo Grove for trading and stablecoin counterparties, Cedar Grove for the CLO purchase, Grove (BVI) for Project Grove. Separate entities per activity class is standard ring-fencing, and it means Grove's counterparty exposure is partitioned in a way the Instance documents never show.

Second, the DAO Resolution is the bridge between the two worlds. A counterparty like FalconX or a CLO issuer cannot contract with a governance process; it contracts with a company. The Resolution is what converts a governance decision into the corporate authority that company needs, which is why each is a separate instrument naming a specific counterparty rather than a general grant.

Third, the list is the legal precondition for the technical one. FalconX appears here as an authorized counterparty and again as the Broker Address routing Grove's Monad allocation; Paxos, Ripple and Agora each have both a Resolution and live Instances. The correspondence is checkable in both directions — and it does not close. Ethena and Wintermute are authorized with no corresponding Instance in the Liquidity Layer, so the Resolution register runs ahead of deployment and reads as a forward indicator of where Grove intends to go next.
description: Seven resolutions empower Grove Foundation, Bamboo Grove Ltd, Cedar Grove Ltd and Grove (BVI) Ltd to onboard with specific counterparties or buy specific securities, each recorded as an IPFS document.
